name: Oval fortified mound with keep and moat, east of Zaranj (Afghan Sistan)
one_line: An 11.5 m oval mound (210 × 135 m) with a 45 m rectangular building on top and a ring about 300 m across around it, like a moat or outer wall. A 70 m square enclosure sits 2.3 km NNW. It has the shape of a Sistan qal'a. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Mud-brick walls, a gate gap in the outer ring, and wind-cut erosion ridges around the base. Rule out a natural yardang reused by modern buildings.
evidence: H3 imagery sweep of the Afghan Sistan corridor; calibrated on Pust-i Gau and Toprak-Kala, which show clearly at 10 m
The area was surveyed by the 1970s Helmand Sistan Project, whose coordinates are not public, so this may be recorded but unpublished

name: Abandoned grid town around a 12.7 m tell, NE of Pust-i Gau (Afghan Sistan)
one_line: A rectilinear grid of compounds covering at least 1 km² around a roughly 200 m mound. Its tone in the short-wave infrared matches the mud-brick walls of Pust-i Gau, 6 km away. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Courtyard houses in a grid, streets, a citadel on the mound, canal lines leading in.
evidence: Probably in the unpublished HSP/Fischer survey lists

name: Square walled enclosure (qal'a?) on a rise, Afghan Sistan
one_line: A crisp 100 m square with thick walls (black in SWIR) and a 30-40 m ring beside it, on an 8.6 m rise. It is either a caravanserai or fort, or a modern compound or security post. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Corner towers and a central courtyard suggest a caravanserai or fort. Vehicles, razor wire or new roofs mean it is modern.

name: Rampart-ringed oval mound in abandoned fields, SE of Pust-i Gau
one_line: A 420 × 270 m oval with a dark raised rim, 8.7 m high in the DEM, sitting among relict strip fields. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A rampart circuit and interior building mounds.

name: Walled oval enclosure on a mound, north of Zaranj (Afghan Sistan)
one_line: The lead's DEM tell finder flagged a 21 ha, 11 m mound. In Sentinel-2 it shows a bounded oval enclosure about 400 m across. This is an independent hit in the same corridor as H1-H4. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: An enclosure wall on the mound.
evidence: Lead's DEM tell finder (it found Tell Brak blind among 242 Khabur tells)

name: Opis (Upi), and possibly Akshak, at Tulul al-Mujaili' on a relict Diyala levee
one_line: Opis was a major Tigris-Diyala city of Babylonian and Persian times. The DEM puts the proposed mound on a NNW-SSE relict levee 15 km NE of Ctesiphon, which splits at a distributary node 6.5 km SSW. The channel link is new; the identification is published. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A 500 × 200 m low mound and the levee ridge running past it.

name: Aratu, a lost Roman road station = the fort at Zawiyet el-Agdab (Egypt)
one_line: Aratu is on the Tabula Peutingeriana but unlocated in the Barrington Atlas. Its road distances (Catabathmus 28, Nesus 26 Roman miles) put the distance-only point in the sea, so the station must lie inland. The only recorded Roman fort within 9 km of the inland solution fits the distances to within 6%.
look_for: A square Roman fort a few tens of metres across.
evidence: H2 missing-station interpolation; the blind test against a known station (Ajdabiya) missed by 5.4 km
The fort is already recorded; the new part is identifying it as Aratu

name: Atil, the Khazar capital, tested at Samosdelka (Volga delta)
one_line: Raised ground on both banks of a 250-300 m channel, with an island at a fork, matches the Arab 'twin city on both banks' layout. Each bank is far smaller than the accounts imply, though, and a 2020 review rejected the identification.
look_for: Settlement ground on both banks of the Staraya Volga channel.

name: Ekallatum zone, 18 km north of Assur: a salvage priority
one_line: Ekallatum was Shamshi-Adad I's royal city. The published '18 km north of Assur, west bank' lands on a terrace-edge town, and no floodplain tell of 4 m or more lies below it. The whole valley is in the Makhul dam reservoir zone, where construction resumed in 2021. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A terrace-edge tell under or beside the modern town.

name: Merrha of Isidore of Charax = Mari (Tell Hariri)?
one_line: Five schoeni below Dura, with the schoenus calibrated on the Dura-Anatho leg, lands 2.6 km from Mari along the river. The name Merrha echoes Mari. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Mari's great tell beside the Euphrates.

name: Zalpuwa 'on the sea' at İkiztepe (Kızılırmak delta)
one_line: An isolated 22 m hill at the inner edge of a delta that held lagoons until about 4,000 years ago, 7.7 km from today's coast. That fits Zalpuwa 'on the sea' in the Old Assyrian era.
look_for: An excavated hill above a flat delta.

name: al-Afa'iya water station on the Darb Zubayda pilgrim road (Saudi Arabia)
one_line: The 32/34-mile interpolation between Mahd adh-Dhahab and Faydat al-Mislah falls 1.25 km from a bright 70-90 m square at the edge of a clay pan. It could be a plastered birka (Abbasid reservoir). (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A square or round stone-lined reservoir with a settling tank. Only 2 of 4 known tanks show at 10 m, so zoom in.

name: Round wooded settlement mounds, central Mali
one_line: The DEM tell finder found a 55 ha, 6 m round mound with a dark wooded cap beside the river. A second one, 85 ha and 12 m, sits at [location withheld]. Their shape is typical of abandoned Middle Niger towns. Regional registers could not be checked. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Pottery-strewn mound surfaces, house-wall rings and erosion gullies.

name: Lost mithraeum of Whitley Castle (Epiacum), Northumberland
one_line: Mithraism was a Roman mystery cult that met in small, half-sunken 'cave' temples. A Mithras altar turned up in 1837 about 91 m east of this fort's north-east corner. At Housesteads, Carrawburgh, Rudchester and Segontium the temple sits 145-342 m out, 6-45 m downslope, in a hollow. That pattern points to the falling ground about 200 m east of the fort. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A damp hollow or terrace on the east slope. Orbit can't see a buried temple; this is a magnetometry or resistivity target.
evidence: M1 pattern fit on four located mithraea

name: Karnasion grove, sanctuary of the Andanian Mysteries (Messenia)
one_line: These were secret initiation rites second only to Eleusis, and their grove has never been located. Pausanias puts it 8 stades (about 1.5 km) from Andania, and the great Mysteries inscription was found 10 minutes' walk from Konstantinoi. Together these favour a spot about 1 km north-west of the published Divari-spring placement. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A spring-fed, wooded valley floor; terrace walls.
evidence: M1 reading of Pausanias 4.33 + the inscription findspot

name: Oracle of Trophonius, the underground oracle of Lebadeia (Greece)
one_line: Consulting this oracle meant a terrifying descent into a narrow underground chamber. Its entrance has never been securely identified. Pausanias's order (grove, then oracle, then a further climb to the temple of Zeus Basileus) plus the elevation profile points to the only level shelf on the ascent. A rival published claim puts it at a well beside the summit temple. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A rock-cut shelf above the Herkyna springs gorge.
evidence: M1 reading of Pausanias 9.39 + DEM profile

name: Göbekli Tepe look-alike knoll, southern Tektek escarpment (Turkey)
one_line: The Taş Tepeler enclosures, with their carved T-shaped pillars, are humanity's oldest known cult centres (about 9600-8000 BC). A terrain score built from the known sites ranks Göbekli Tepe itself in the top 1.5% of 2,193 regional knolls. This knoll, 11 km south of Harbetsuvan on the same escarpment as Kurt, Karahan and Harbetsuvan, has the radial profile closest to Göbekli's of the 38 examined. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: A soft, rounded artificial-looking mound and rows of protruding stone slab tops at full zoom.
evidence: M1 knoll scoring calibrated on known sites

name: Plateau summit between the Euphrates sites and the Taş Tepeler group
one_line: A soil-capped summit on the Birecik-Suruç plateau, in the survey gap between the Euphrates PPNA sites and the western Taş Tepeler cluster. Of the summits examined, its tone pattern is the most like Göbekli's. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: As S4.

name: Vindolanda's missing mithraeum (Hadrian's Wall)
one_line: Vindolanda is the best-studied fort on the Wall, yet no Mithras temple has been found there. Pattern scoring picks the stream hollows 150-170 m out and about 10 m below the fort. (Location rounded to about 10 km in the public copy.)
look_for: Geophysics target; nothing visible from orbit.

name: Jonestown, Peoples Temple settlement (Guyana), historical context
one_line: This was the site of the 1978 mass murder-suicide. Forest has reclaimed it; only a track shows at 10 m.
look_for: Clearings and the airstrip at Port Kaituma further north.

name: Rajneeshpuram / Big Muddy Ranch (Oregon), historical context
one_line: The 1980s commune of the Rajneesh movement, which was behind the 1984 salmonella attack. It is now a youth camp, and its buildings and reservoir are still clear from orbit.
look_for: The town grid along the creek.

name: Colonia Dignidad / Villa Baviera (Chile), historical context
one_line: Paul Schäfer's sealed German enclave, used as a torture site under Pinochet. It sits clearly visible on the Perquilauquén river.
look_for: The compound buildings beside the river.
